items.followUp: Two masses of 3 kg and 5 kg are connected over a frictionless pulley. Describe their motion and find their acceleration in terms of g.

rubric.why: Describes the directions of motion and the acceleration constraint for the connected bodies.
rubric.description: States that the heavier mass moves down, the lighter mass moves up, and both have equal-magnitude acceleration.
rubric.how: Award for all three features: relative mass, directions, and equal-magnitude acceleration.

rubric.why: Applies Newton’s second law to each mass in its direction of motion.
rubric.description: Writes the equations of motion for the heavier and lighter masses.

rubric.why: Gives the resulting acceleration of the system.
rubric.description: Obtains the acceleration in terms of the two masses and g.
rubric.how: Award for the correct acceleration expression.

rubric.why: Gives the tension in the connecting string.
rubric.description: Obtains the string tension for the ideal pulley system.
rubric.how: Award for the correct tension expression.

modelAnswer: Let the masses be m2 and m1, with m2 > m1. The heavier mass moves downward and the lighter mass moves upward.
Because the string is taut and the pulley is frictionless, both masses have the same magnitude of acceleration, a, and the tension T is the same on both sides.
For m2 moving downward: m2g − T = m2a.
For m1 moving upward: T − m1g = m1a.
Adding the equations gives the acceleration: a = (m2 − m1)g/(m1 + m2).
